title: Top three routes per airline
statementMd:
For each airline, rank routes (origin, destination) by number of flights and show the top route with its count (ties: alphabetical origin then destination).

Expected columns: `airline_code`, `origin`, `destination`, `flights`.

Tables: `airlines`, `airports`, `flights`, `bookings`.

Row order does not matter.
solutionMd:
```sql
WITH r AS (SELECT airline_code, origin, destination, COUNT(*) AS flights FROM flights GROUP BY airline_code, origin, destination), k AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY airline_code ORDER BY flights DESC, origin, destination) AS rn FROM r) SELECT airline_code, origin, destination, flights FROM k WHERE rn = 1;
```

Compare with your own query; the result sets must match.
